title: Conditions, loops, methods, parameters, return values, and exceptions
objectives: Choose if-else or switch versus a loop when Apex must branch or repeat.
Name the five Apex loop forms and when break or continue applies.
Define a method with a return type or void, parameters (max 32), and a body.
Use throw, try, catch, and finally so an exception is handled without swallowing every failure.
diagnostic_question: A helper must skip closed LAB_ Case rows, stop after the first match, return an Id or null, and still close a logging resource if a query fails. Which combination of condition, loop, method signature, and try/catch/finally would you sketch before typing?
definition: Apex control flow uses if-else, switch, and five loop forms so statements are not only line-by-line. Methods declare a return type or void, up to 32 parameters, and a body. Exceptions interrupt normal flow: throw signals failure; try, catch, and finally recover or clean up. ([Control Flow](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/langCon_apex_control_flow.htm); [Class Methods](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_defining_methods.htm); [Exception Statements](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_exception_statements.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers listen for bulk-safe loops (no SOQL inside a for-each over Trigger.new), honest return types instead of magic strings, and catch blocks that do not hide DML failures. Mixing Flow decision diamonds with Apex if without knowing try/finally is a common fail.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a railway signal box. A condition is a switch: this track or that track. A loop is a repeating circuit until the exit signal. A method is a named timetable procedure: parameters are the consist handed in, the return value is the consist handed out, void means the procedure only throws switches. An exception is the emergency stop; catch is the recovery siding; finally is the rule that you still lock the box even if the train never arrived.
deeper_explanation: Statements normally run in order. If-else and switch branch; loops repeat. Apex documents five procedural loops: do-while, while, three-part for, for-each over an array or set, and for-each over an inline SOQL query. All loops support break (exit the loop) and continue (next iteration). ([Control Flow](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/langCon_apex_control_flow.htm); [Loops](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/langCon_apex_loops.htm))

A method needs optional modifiers, a return data type or void, a parenthesized parameter list, and a brace body. A method may have at most 32 input parameters. Methods can be overloaded; the parser picks an exact match then approximate conversion. ([Class Methods](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_defining_methods.htm))

throw raises an exception object. try marks the risky block. Each catch handles one unique exception type; a general Exception catch must be last. finally always runs for cleanup. At least one catch or finally must be present with try. ([Exception Statements](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_exception_statements.htm))

This lesson is control-flow vocabulary before Apex bulk patterns. Putting SOQL or DML inside a loop over Trigger.new is an anti-pattern owned by later governor topics. Empty catch blocks that ignore DML exceptions are not 'handling'.

mental_model.analogy: Railway signal box: switches (conditions), repeating circuits (loops), named timetable procedures (methods with parameters and return values), emergency stop and recovery siding (exceptions).
useful_mapping: if-else / switch → which track the consist takes
loop → a circuit repeated until the exit signal
continue → skip to the next lap
method → a named procedure on the timetable
parameters → cars handed into the procedure
return value → cars handed back; void means no consist returned
throw / catch / finally → emergency stop, recovery siding, always lock the box
where_it_breaks: Real railways do not have a 32-parameter cap.
SOQL-for loops are not physical tracks; they query data.
finally is not optional safety theater—the guide says it always executes.
The analogy does not encode governor limits or trigger bulkification.

teach_back_prompt: Using the signal box, explain if versus a for-each loop, what void means on a method, and why a catch (Exception e) must be last. Then say where the railway analogy breaks.

review_schedule.prompt: List five Apex loop types and the difference between break and continue.
Write a method signature with two parameters and a String return; then a void method that only logs.
Sketch try/catch/finally for a query that must still run cleanup.
Review a loop that queries inside Trigger.new and explain the control-flow versus bulk mistake.
Two-minute interview: conditions, loops, methods, parameters, returns, exceptions.

mermaid.structure:
flowchart TD
  Start[Sequential statements] --> Branch{Condition if or switch}
  Branch -->|Match| PathA[One path]
  Branch -->|Else| PathB[Other path]
  PathA --> Loop[Loop while or for]
  PathB --> Loop
  Loop --> Method[Method: parameters in, return or void out]
  Method --> Ok[Normal return]
  Method --> Throw[throw exception]
  Throw --> Catch[Matching catch]
  Catch --> Finally[finally always]
  Ok --> Finally

claims.claim: Apex provides if-else statements, switch statements, and loops to control execution. Statements otherwise run in source order.
Apex supports five procedural loops: do-while, while, three-part for, for-each over an array or set, and for-each over inline SOQL. break exits the loop; continue skips to the next iteration.
claims.validation: Loops page in the Apex Developer Guide.

claims.claim: A method requires a return type or void, a name, parentheses with at most 32 parameters, and a body. Methods may be overloaded.
throw signals an error. try/catch/finally recover: catch types must be unique, a general Exception catch must be last, and finally always executes. try needs at least a catch or a finally.

changed_in_release: Control-flow and exception syntax here is stable in Summer '26 (API 67.0). Reverify switch value types against the current guide if you rely on a new type.
unresolved_uncertainty: Exact switch-supported types can be version-sensitive; confirm on the Switch Statements page before an interview deep-dive.

telugu_glossary.telugu: పేరున్న పని; ఇన్‌పుట్ పారామితులు, రిటర్న్ లేదా void.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Conditions branch, loops repeat—Apex has five loop forms plus break and continue. Methods take up to 32 parameters and return a type or void. Exceptions use throw, try, catch, and finally; empty catch is not handling.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I pick if or switch for a one-time decision and a loop when work repeats. for-each over a list is the usual collection walk; SOQL-for is for query rows. I extract a method when the work has a name, inputs, and a return. I catch specific types first and Exception last. finally is for cleanup that must run. I do not put queries inside a loop over Trigger.new in this foundation lesson—that is a bulk/governor fail later.

terminology.plain: A yes/no (or multi-way) choice that picks which statements run.
terminology.precise: if-else or switch: Apex branches instead of running every line in order.
terminology.non_example: A validation rule on the object is not an Apex if statement.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Flow Decision element: declarative branching, not Apex syntax.
terminology.boundary: Formula IF() is a different expression language.

terminology.plain: A block that repeats while a condition holds or while items remain.
terminology.precise: Five forms: do-while, while, three-part for, for (x : listOrSet), for (x : [SOQL]). break exits; continue skips one iteration.
terminology.non_example: A scheduled job is not itself a language loop.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Batch Apex execute chunks: platform batching, not a while loop you wrote.
terminology.boundary: Governor-safe bulk loops are APEX-007; this lesson is the syntax.

terminology.plain: A named procedure a class can run.
terminology.precise: Optional modifiers, required return type or void, up to 32 parameters, brace body. Can be overloaded.
terminology.example: public static Id labFirstOpen(List<Case> rows) { ... return rows[0].Id; }
terminology.non_example: A Flow Action is not an Apex method unless it invokes one.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Constructor: initializer, not a general method with a return type.
terminology.boundary: Access modifiers are APEX-001; this lesson is signature and control flow.

terminology.plain: An input slot the caller fills when invoking the method.
terminology.precise: Each parameter has a type and name. Maximum 32 input parameters per method.
terminology.non_example: A URL query string on a REST call is not an Apex method parameter until you map it.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Return value: output of the method, not an input.
terminology.boundary: Pass-by-value details are on the Class Methods page; do not invent Java-memory diagrams.

terminology.plain: The typed result handed back to the caller, or nothing if void.
terminology.precise: The method's data type is required. Use void when the method does not return a value. Callers may ignore a non-void result, as in Java.
terminology.example: return labId; versus public void labLog() { }
terminology.non_example: System.debug is a side effect, not a return value unless you return the string.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Exception: failure path, not a normal return.
terminology.boundary: Future methods returning void is APEX-011, not this lesson's general rule.

terminology.plain: A disruption of normal execution you can throw or catch.
terminology.precise: throw an exception object. try/catch/finally recover. Catch types unique; Exception last; finally always runs.
terminology.example: try { insert labAcc; } catch (DmlException e) { ... } finally { labCleanup(); }
terminology.non_example: A Flow fault connector is not an Apex catch block.
terminology.boundary: Custom exception classes and built-in types are expanded in APEX-006.

terminology.plain: Cleanup that runs whether the try succeeded or failed.
terminology.precise: A try may have at most one finally. It always executes regardless of exception type. Use it to free resources.
terminology.non_example: A second catch is not finally.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: catch: handles a type; finally: always runs.
terminology.boundary: Do not use finally to hide a failed DML by ignoring it.

terminology.plain: Two methods with the same name and different parameter lists.
terminology.precise: The parser selects the exact match, then conversion. Multiple approximate matches cause a parse-time exception.
terminology.example: labAdd(Integer i) and labAdd(Integer i, Integer j)
terminology.non_example: Two methods that differ only by return type are not a valid overload story—Needs verification of exact Apex overload-by-return rules; prefer different parameter lists.
terminology.boundary: Do not overload @AuraEnabled methods for LWC (later LWC topic).

mechanics.trigger: Logic is not a straight line
mechanics.after: if/switch for a decision, a loop for repetition
mechanics.failure: Copy-pasted blocks instead of a loop

mechanics.trigger: The same work needs inputs and a result
mechanics.after: Typed parameters, return or void, body under 32 params
mechanics.failure: Returning a magic String 'ERR' instead of throwing or a typed result

mechanics.trigger: DML, query, or invariant can fail
mechanics.after: Specific catch, Exception last if needed, finally for cleanup
mechanics.observe: Tests assert the catch path; cleanup still runs
mechanics.failure: catch (Exception e) { } with an empty body

mechanics.before: Query inside the loop looks convenient
mechanics.after: Collection loop without per-iteration SOQL/DML (later governors)
mechanics.observe: One query before the loop in the lab
mechanics.failure: for (Account a : Trigger.new) { List<Contact> c = [SELECT Id FROM Contact WHERE AccountId = :a.Id]; }

when_to_use: When you must branch with conditions or repeat with loops in Apex rather than a one-line assignment.
When extracting a method with parameters and a return value or void so callers share one body.
When an exception must be thrown, caught, or cleaned up with finally instead of crashing silently.
When a review asks whether a for-each, while, or SOQL-for loop is the right repetition form.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this conditions-and-loops lesson as a substitute for governor bulkification numbers (APEX-007).
Do not treat methods and parameters as the access-modifier lesson (private/public/global is APEX-001).
Do not catch Exception empty-handed to 'make the test pass' while hiding DML failures.
Do not replace a Flow Decision with Apex if a declarative condition already meets the requirement (AUTO-001).
configuration_or_code_location: Apex class methods in a sandbox; Developer Console anonymous Apex for tiny loop labs.
Method header: return type, name, parameter list.
try/catch/finally wrapping DML or queries in the same method.
Problems pane for 'variable does not exist' after a return or break.

worked_example.scenario: Sandbox class LAB_CasePicker receives a list of synthetic Case rows. It must skip closed cases, return the first open Id, return null if none, and still run a finally block that records that the method finished. No production data.
inputs: List<Case> that may be empty or mixed open/closed
Need a reusable method, not anonymous-only
Cleanup flag must flip even when the list is null

decisions.decision: Use a for-each loop over the list with continue on closed rows and break after the first open Id.
decisions.because: Loops page: for (variable : array_or_set), continue skips, break exits.
decisions.rejected: A while(true) with a manual index for a simple list walk

decisions.decision: Method signature Id pick(List<Case> rows) returning null when none match.
decisions.because: Class Methods require a return type; Id or null is honest versus a magic String.
decisions.rejected: void method that writes to a public static as a hidden return

decisions.decision: try/catch NullPointerException for a null list, finally sets labDone = true.
decisions.because: finally always executes; catch types should be specific.

configuration_or_code: public class LAB_CasePicker { public static Boolean labDone; public static Id pick(List<Case> rows) { labDone = false; Id found; try { for (Case c : rows) { if (c.IsClosed) { continue; } found = c.Id; break; } } catch (NullPointerException e) { found = null; } finally { labDone = true; } return found; } }
Call pick(null) and assert labDone is true.
Call pick with one closed and one open Case and assert the open Id.
worked_example.output: First open Id or null; labDone true after both success and null-list paths.
verification: Null list: return null and labDone true.
Closed-only list: return null after continue on each row.
Empty catch is absent from the class.
worked_example.self_explanation: The loop skipped closed rows, the method returned a typed Id, and finally still ran.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable sandbox or scratch org; LAB_ Apex only.
starting_state_checks: Can create Apex classes and run tests or anonymous Apex.
steps: Create LAB_CasePicker with pick(List<Case> rows) using for-each, continue, break, and a typed Id return.
Add try/catch/finally so a null list does not skip the finally flag.
Write a test or anonymous asserts for empty list, null list, and mixed closed/open rows.
Intentionally add a 33rd parameter to a dummy method and capture the compile error, then revert.
guided_completion: If finally did not run on null, the catch swallowed the method before finally—or you returned inside catch incorrectly. Recheck the guide: finally always executes.
If you queried inside the loop, remove that query for this lab.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: Overload pick with pick(List<Case> rows, String status) and explain how the parser chooses an overload.
evidence: Test or anonymous output for null list still setting the finally flag.
Compile error text for too many parameters, then the reverted 2-parameter method.
hands_on_lab.limitations: Does not prove built-in exception class catalogs or trigger bulk patterns.

decision_table.signal: One business decision with two or a few named paths.
decision_table.choose: if-else or switch condition, not a loop.
decision_table.not: A for loop that happens to run once.
decision_table.why: Control flow page: conditions branch; loops repeat.

decision_table.signal: Walk every element of an in-memory list or set.
decision_table.choose: for (Type x : collection) with continue/break as needed.
decision_table.not: while with a handwritten index unless you truly need the index.
decision_table.why: The Loops page lists for-each over array_or_set as a first-class form.

decision_table.signal: Reusable work with inputs and a result for callers.
decision_table.choose: A method with typed parameters and a return type or void.
decision_table.not: Copy-paste the block, or more than 32 parameters.
decision_table.why: Class Methods require a signature and cap parameters at 32.

decision_table.signal: An operation can fail and you still must clean up.
decision_table.choose: try with a specific catch and a finally block.
decision_table.not: Empty catch (Exception e) that hides the failure.
decision_table.why: Exception Statements: finally always runs; catch types should be unique and Exception last.

limitations: Does not catalog every built-in exception type.
Does not teach Queueable versus future.
Does not replace Flow Decision design.
32-parameter cap is from the methods guide; do not invent other numeric limits here.
security_notes: Do not log exception messages that contain secrets or personal data.
Empty catch can hide authorization failures; treat that as a security smell.
Parameters from users still need CRUD/FLS later (APEX-015).
common_mistakes: SOQL inside a loop over Trigger.new.
Using String return codes instead of throw or a typed return.
Putting Exception catch before a more specific catch.
Confusing break (leave loop) with return (leave method).

check: Did every path return or throw?
Did break versus return get mixed up?
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The compiler is wrong about reachability.

troubleshooting.symptom: finally did not seem to run.
check: Is there a try with finally?
Did the process die at the platform limit rather than an Apex catch?

troubleshooting.symptom: Compile error about too many parameters.
check: Count the input parameters; the cap is 32.
Group inputs in a small class instead of a long list.

production_notes: Do not ship empty catch blocks.
Sandbox-test exception paths, not only the happy return.
This lesson does not authorize production anonymous Apex with DML.

mcqs.prompt: How many procedural loop types does the Apex Loops page list?
mcqs.rationale: do-while, while, three-part for, for-each collection, and for-each SOQL.

distractor_explanations.B: Those exist, but they are not the full list.

mcqs.prompt: What is the maximum number of input parameters on an Apex method?
mcqs.rationale: Class Methods: a method can only have 32 input parameters.

mcqs.prompt: A method should not hand a value back to the caller. What return type?

options.D: Omit the return type entirely like JavaScript

mcqs.rationale: Use void if the method does not return a value.

distractor_explanations.B: null is a value, not a return type.
distractor_explanations.C: Object is a type, not the void marker.
distractor_explanations.D: Apex requires a return type or void.

mcqs.prompt: Where must a catch (Exception e) appear relative to other catch blocks?

options.C: It cannot be used in Apex

mcqs.rationale: The general Exception type must be the last catch block when used.

mcqs.prompt: What does continue do in an Apex loop?
mcqs.rationale: continue skips to the next iteration; break exits the loop.

distractor_explanations.D: That is DML exception / rollback behavior, not continue.

mcqs.prompt: Does finally run if a catch block handled the exception?
mcqs.rationale: Code in finally always executes regardless of whether an exception was thrown or which type.

mcqs.prompt: You need to walk query results without first assigning a List. Which loop form is documented for that?
mcqs.rationale: The fifth loop form is for-each over an inline SOQL query.

distractor_explanations.B: switch is not a query walker.

mcqs.prompt: A catch (Exception e) {} empty block 'fixes' a failing insert in a demo. Risk?

options.A: It hides the DML failure and is not graceful recovery

mcqs.rationale: try/catch is for recovery, not for swallowing errors. Empty catch hides failures.

mcqs.prompt: if-else versus a loop: which statement is accurate?

options.A: Conditions branch once; loops repeat a block
options.D: if-else is only allowed in triggers

mcqs.rationale: Control flow: execute based on a condition, or repeat a block.

mcqs.prompt: break versus return inside a loop in a method?

options.A: break leaves the loop; return leaves the method
options.C: return only works in void methods

mcqs.rationale: Loops page: break exits the loop. return is a method exit with an optional value.

distractor_explanations.C: void methods can return; with no value.
distractor_explanations.D: break does not return a typed value.

mcqs.prompt: Two methods named labAdd, one with one Integer and one with two. What is this?

options.A: Overloading; the parser picks by parameter list

mcqs.rationale: User-defined methods can be overloaded; the parser selects the implementation.

mcqs.prompt: A try block has no catch and no finally. Valid?

options.A: No; at least a catch or a finally must be present
options.D: Only if the method is void

mcqs.rationale: Exception Statements: at least the catch block or the finally block must be present.

No. Do not log credentials, session IDs, or personal data.

interview_questions.question: Explain conditions, loops, methods, parameters, return values, and exceptions in Apex.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Conditions branch, five loop forms repeat, methods take up to 32 parameters and return a type or void, exceptions use throw plus try/catch/finally.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use if or switch for a decision and a loop when work repeats. I name the five loop types and break versus continue. A method is a signature: return or void, parameters, body. I catch specific exceptions first and put Exception last. finally always runs. I do not call an empty catch 'error handling'.
interview_questions.example: LAB_CasePicker: for-each, continue on closed, break on first Id, finally sets a done flag.
tradeoffs: Typed return vs void plus side effects
follow_ups: Does finally run after return in try?

interview_questions.question: What mistakes do beginners make with Apex loops and exceptions?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: SOQL in a loop, empty catch, mixing up break and return, and treating void as optional syntax.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The loop syntax can be correct and still be a bulk failure. Empty catch hides DML. catch (Exception e) before a specific type is illegal/wrong. Methods need a return type. I also see while(true) without a guaranteed break. I separate this lesson from governor numbers but I still refuse per-row queries.
interview_questions.example: for (Account a : Trigger.new) { Contact c = [SELECT Id FROM Contact WHERE AccountId = :a.Id]; } is the classic fail.
tradeoffs: Convenient per-row query vs bulk-safe collections
follow_ups: How would you rewrite that loop?
weak_answer_warnings: Saying governors do not apply in sandbox

interview_questions.question: Design a method that returns the first open Case Id from a list or null.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Id pick(List<Case> rows) with for-each, continue if closed, break after the first open Id, return found.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Signature returns Id, not String. Null list is either a precondition check or a caught NPE; either way finally can mark completion. I would not use a void method that sets a static. I would not query inside the loop if the list is already in memory. Overload only if a second parameter list is truly needed.
interview_questions.example: LAB_CasePicker.pick in the worked example with labDone in finally.
tradeoffs: null return vs custom exception when none found
follow_ups: When would you throw instead of return null?

interview_questions.question: You must always close a debug buffer whether insert succeeds or fails. Structure?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: try the insert, catch DmlException specifically, put close() in finally so it always runs.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: try identifies the risky DML. catch (DmlException e) handles that type. I do not start with Exception unless I also keep it last. finally closes the buffer because the guide says it always executes. I still surface or log the error; I do not empty-catch. If the platform kills the transaction via an unhandleable governor, I say that is outside this finally guarantee—Needs verification for limit exceptions that cannot be caught.
interview_questions.example: try { insert labAcc; } catch (DmlException e) { labLog(e); } finally { labBuf.close(); }
tradeoffs: Rethrow after log vs swallow after compensate
follow_ups: Can governor limit exceptions be caught?
weak_answer_warnings: Putting close() only in the success path

interview_questions.question: Compile error: catch block is unreachable. What do you look at?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A broader Exception catch is probably above a more specific catch, or two catches share a type.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The guide requires unique catch types and Exception last. I reorder catches from specific to general. I also check I did not duplicate DmlException. This is not a missing import. I recompile after the reorder and add a test that throws the specific type.
interview_questions.example: catch (Exception e) before catch (DmlException e) is the usual order bug.
tradeoffs: One broad catch vs several specific catches
follow_ups: Must you have a catch if you have finally?
What does unique catch type mean?

interview_questions.question: A loop never stops. How do you diagnose with this vocabulary?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check the while/do-while Boolean, missing increment in a three-part for, and missing break on the success condition.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Infinite loops are usually while (true) without break, or a condition that never becomes false. for-each over a list cannot grow forever unless the list is mutated in a surprising way—I would inspect mutation. I distinguish 'loop never stops' from 'method never returns' (missing return on some if path). I do not jump to governors first if CPU has not yet been mentioned.
interview_questions.example: while (i < 10) { /* forgot i++ */ } versus for (Case c : rows) which is bounded by list size.
tradeoffs: do-while (runs once) vs while (may run zero times)
follow_ups: When is do-while the right form?
How does continue hide a missing increment?
weak_answer_warnings: Calling it a Salesforce platform outage

interview_questions.question: When would you avoid a method and keep the condition inline?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the branch is a single obvious check used once and a method would only hide a one-liner.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I extract a method when there are parameters, a return value, reuse, or an exception policy to test. I keep inline if-else for a local flag. I avoid a 32-parameter method by grouping inputs. I also avoid Apex entirely if a Flow Decision is enough—this track is still programming foundations, not an excuse to code every condition.
interview_questions.example: if (rows == null) return null; stays inline; pick-first-open-Id becomes a method.
tradeoffs: Readability of a named method vs local clarity
follow_ups: What about overloading instead of a Boolean flag parameter?
When is switch clearer than if-else?

interview_questions.question: Teach this topic with the railway signal box and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Switches are conditions, repeating circuits are loops, timetable procedures are methods, emergency stop is throw, finally locks the box. It breaks on the 32-parameter cap and governors.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I walk a consist through a switch (if), around a circuit (for-each), into a named procedure with cars in and cars out (parameters and return), then an emergency stop (throw) onto a recovery siding (catch) while still locking the box (finally). I then say railways have no 32-parameter rule, SOQL-for is not a physical track, and empty catch is not recovery. I finish with two lines of Apex.
interview_questions.example: Show continue on closed cases as 'skip this car' and break as 'leave the circuit'.
